findings.description: Case 1 of the precedence, re-derived in a scratch cwd outside this repo: with a fixture .agent-guild/state/spec.md carrying ref "acme/widgets#999" and no --job flag, the written ledger line carries that ref.
findings.evidence: cwd=/private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/c2, ran /Users/k.arnett/repos/agent-guild/.agent-guild/scripts/ledger-append.py with no --job; raw line read back from c2/.agent-guild/state/log/vendor-calls.jsonl: {"task_id": "T-999", ..., "quota_event": false, "job": "acme/widgets#999"} (rc 0, empty stderr). Fixture header line was: ref: "acme/widgets#999" — the one matching quote pair is stripped.

findings.description: Case 2: the same fixture spec plus --job override/from#flag writes the flag's value, so the flag wins outright over the derivable provenance ref.
findings.evidence: Same scratch cwd, extra argv ['--job', 'override/from#flag']; raw line: {..., "quota_event": false, "job": "override/from#flag"} — the spec's "acme/widgets#999" is present on disk and does not appear in the line.

findings.description: Case 3, the discriminating one: with no spec.md anywhere under the scratch cwd, the line omits the job key entirely rather than emitting null, and does not fall back to this repo's spec — confirming the path resolves against cwd, not the script's own location.
findings.evidence: Scratch spec.md removed (os.path.exists -> False); raw line: {"task_id": "T-999", ..., "artifacts": [], "quota_event": false} with no job key ('job' in obj -> False). This repo's .agent-guild/state/spec.md carries `ref: /Users/k.arnett/.claude/plans/lets-fix-gh-issue-tidy-cook.md`, so a script-relative resolution would have emitted that string as job and silently passed; it did not.

findings.description: The cwd assumption is explicit in the source: SPEC_PATH is built from os.getcwd() alongside DEFAULT_LEDGER, deliberately not from SCRIPT_DIR (which is used only to locate the schema).
findings.evidence: .agent-guild/scripts/ledger-append.py:60-70 — SCRIPT_DIR/SCHEMA_PATH at 60-63, then DEFAULT_LEDGER at 64-66 and `SPEC_PATH = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".agent-guild", "state", "spec.md")` at line 70, with the comment at 67-69 naming the copied-into-other-projects reason.

findings.description: The schema carries job under properties typed string and keeps it out of required, so a pre-change row with no job key still validates.
findings.evidence: .agent-guild/schemas/vendor-call.schema.json:60-63 (job in properties, "type": "string") and :65-79 (required lists 13 fields, no job). Read programmatically: job under properties: True / job type: 'string' / job in required: False. Validating a legacy 13-key row via this repo's load_schema()+schema_violation() returned None.

findings.description: No code path can emit "job": null — the key is assigned only under an `is not None` guard, and an empty or missing ref collapses to None upstream, so absence is the only spelling of unattributed.
findings.evidence: .agent-guild/scripts/ledger-append.py:212-216 — `job = args.job if args.job is not None else derive_job()` then `if job is not None: line["job"] = job`; this is the sole write to line["job"] (grep -n 'job' shows assignments only at 214/216). derive_job returns None on OSError (161-163), on a missing/!--- header (166-167, 180), and returns `val or None` at 179. Belt and braces, the schema rejects it anyway: schema_violation({...,'job':None}) -> ('job', 'expected type string, got null (None)').

findings.description: The new ref reader strips at most one matching quote pair using the val[0] == val[-1] form, character-for-character the same guard compose-brief.py and check-provenance.py already use.
findings.evidence: .agent-guild/scripts/ledger-append.py:177-178 — `if len(val) >= 2 and val[0] == val[-1] and val[0] in "\"'":` / `val = val[1:-1]`; identical text at .agent-guild/scripts/compose-brief.py:64-65 and .agent-guild/scripts/check-provenance.py:74-75.

findings.description: No character-set strip appears anywhere in the file: every strip() call is a bare whitespace strip, and the #127 defect is called out by name in a comment rather than reintroduced.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'strip(' .agent-guild/scripts/ledger-append.py returns only lines 166, 169, 174 (all bare `.strip()`) plus the comment at 175-176 ("never str.strip(\"'\\\"\"), which trims any number of quote characters regardless of balance (#127)"). Behavior re-derived by calling derive_job on six fixture headers: 'ref: "x#9"' -> 'x#9'; "ref: 'x#9'" -> 'x#9'; 'ref: "x#9' -> '"x#9' (unbalanced leading quote kept); 'ref: x#9"' -> 'x#9"' (unbalanced trailing quote kept); 'ref: ""x#9""' -> '"x#9"' (exactly one pair removed); 'ref: x#9' -> 'x#9'.
